Fetches OVAL (Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language) security data files from Red Hat's security data portal, supporting both OVAL v1 (archived tar.gz) and OVAL v2 (individual bzip2) formats across RHEL versions 4–9+.

## Key Components

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `FetchFiles(versions []string)` | Main entry point; routes each RHEL version to the appropriate OVAL fetcher and aggregates results |
| `fetchOVALv1(names []string)` | Downloads the archived `oval_v1_20230706.tar.gz` and extracts named XML files for RHEL 4–9 |
| `fetchOVALv2(names []string)` | Downloads individual bzip2-compressed OVAL v2 XML files per stream (e.g. `including-unpatched`, `extras`, `els`) |

### Version Routing Logic

| RHEL Version | Behavior |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Skipped — no vulnerability data provided |
| 4 | OVALv1 only |
| 5 | OVALv1 (main + ELS) |
| 6 | OVALv1 + OVALv2 (including-unpatched, extras, supplementary, els) |
| 7 | OVALv1 + OVALv2 (including-unpatched, extras, supplementary) |
| 8–9 | OVALv1 + OVALv2 (including-unpatched) |
| 10+ (numeric) | OVALv2 only |

## Usage Example

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "github.com/vulsio/goval-dictionary/fetcher/redhat"
)

func main() {
    results, err := redhat.FetchFiles([]string{"8", "9"})
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }

    for version, fetchResults := range results {
        fmt.Printf("RHEL %s: %d OVAL feed(s) fetched\n", version, len(fetchResults))
        for _, r := range fetchResults {
            fmt.Printf("  Target: %s | URL: %s\n", r.Target, r.URL)
        }
    }
}
```
